sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of Lightweight Ad-Monetized Mobile Games

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European system, substantially influenced by French Code Civil and German legal doctrine)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1996, encouraging and protecting reciprocal investments)
Luxembourg–United States Treaty of Friendship, Establishment and Navigation (1963)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing a Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law), as amended; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD4 and AMLD5), as transposed

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency of each direct and indirect corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Commerce or competent corporate registry of the jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of valid passport of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) and each manager (dirigeant)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary, municipal authority, or competent government office of the holder's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or recent official extract of the corporate register of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation of the shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French or German translation of all non-Luxembourg constitutive documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator admitted by the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice or by the competent court of the origin state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization where Hague Apostille is not recognized

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory electronic screening of all UBOs, shareholders, managers, and authorized signatories against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, UK HMT consolidated list, and the Luxembourg national asset-freezing list published by the Ministry of Finance; mandatory Politically Exposed Person (PEP) identification and enhanced due diligence in accordance with CSSF Regulation 12-02 and Article 3 of Directive (EU) 2015/849; ongoing transaction monitoring and adverse-media screening aligned to the Hyper-Casual Games payout rails (AdMob and AppLovin)

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS electronic filing portal via www.lbr.lu and the Guichet.lu single point of filing (eJustice module)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must include the legal form suffix 'SARL' or 'Société à responsabilité limitée'; only Latin-alphabet characters are accepted in the registered name; a French, German, or Luxembourgish transliteration is strongly recommended for the commercial trade name, while foreign words are permitted provided the name remains clearly distinguishable from existing RCS registrations and is not misleading as to the company's activity or legal form
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed corporate name, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the RCS registrar through the LBR/Guichet.lu portal within 15 days of the rejection notice, providing justification and, where appropriate, a modified name for immediate re-deposit; if the initial refusal is maintained, a formal administrative appeal may be lodged with the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) in commercial matters within one month of notification under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies; extension of an approved name reservation beyond 30 days may be granted by the Registrar upon written justification before the expiry date

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A foreign or purely virtual address outside Luxembourg is not permissible; the SARL must maintain a genuine registered office within Luxembourg as stated in its articles of association. For low-risk standard industries such as hyper-casual mobile gaming, a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent may provide a registered business address and administrative mail-handling services, provided the company retains a contractual seat and accounting substance in Luxembourg; full back-office virtualisation without any physical Luxembourg presence is not compliant with substance expectations
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for this industry: quantified unannounced on-site inspection probability of approximately 5% per year for a newly incorporated low-risk standard SARL in the software publishing sector; the probability increases substantially if the company fails statutory filing deadlines, exhibits inconsistent substance indicators, or triggers CSSF, tax administration, or AML/CFT risk alerts

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and reservation of corporate name at Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR / RCS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory exemption — electronic name pre-clearance is free of charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial drafting of articles of association and incorporation deed (notarial deed in French language)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EUR 2,000–2,500 for a standard SARL with one manager and one corporate or natural shareholder, inclusive of escrow of minimum capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration and statutory publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers and Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry and publication tariff (approximately EUR 150–190 per filing)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular authentication of foreign corporate and UBO documents (up to 5 instruments)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs of Luxembourg or competent authority of the origin state
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document statutory consular fee of EUR 20–60 per apostille or legalization

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation of constitutive documents (certified French translation of corporate charters, certificates of incumbency, and passports)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator licensed by the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 100–150 per page for certified legal translations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT KYC bundle compilation, UBO RBE filing threshold review, and sanctions screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate service provider or registered agent admitted in Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing service-provider benchmark of EUR 300–400 for the AML onset module, including PEP and sanctions checks

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Domiciliation agreement for registered office in Luxembourg (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg domiciliation agent licensed by the Ministry of Economy
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 900–1,200 per year for low-risk standard domiciliation without dedicated physical staffing

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 710-1 to 710-30 governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); combined with the Law of 11 January 2008 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) and the Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS and company accounts, as amended
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), under the supervision of the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (notarial deed of incorporation) executed by a Luxembourg civil-law notary and filed electronically via the eRCS portal; thereafter published as a communication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 minimum share capital for an SARL, fully subscribed and fully paid in cash before signature of the notarial deed; the contribution must be deposited into a blocked escrow account opened in the name of the société en formation with an EU/EEA credit institution, evidenced by an attestation de blocage issued to the notary; the funds are released only after RCS registration confers legal personality
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the fully subscribed and paid-up share capital of EUR 12,000, comprising 12,000 registered shares of EUR 1.00 each, is hereby ratified and allotted to the subscribers. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is fixed at [Registered Office Address], Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed sole Manager (Gérant) with full authority to bind the Company, open bank accounts, execute agreements, hire staff, and manage all day-to-day operations of the hyper-casual mobile game publishing business. RESOLVED, that the Manager is authorized to complete all statutory registrations, RCS updates, tax and VAT filings, and banking onboarding documents, and to take every act necessary to commence business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name availability check and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), eRCS online portal at lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a name-availability search on the RCS electronic database and file an online name-reservation application for a distinctive name ending with the legal-form suffix 'SARL'. The RCS verifies non-conflict, distinctiveness, and non-misleading character. Reservation, if granted, is valid for three months and may be renewed. Name reservation is optional but strongly recommended for hyper-casual gaming brand clarity.
required_dossiers: Online name-reservation application form
Proposed corporate name including 'SARL' suffix
Identity document of the applicant founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused for lack of distinctiveness or conflict, refile with a stronger distinctive element (e.g., a coined brand suffix). If the RCS maintains the refusal, appeal to the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within one month of formal notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and notarial approval of draft articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Chamber of Notaries and licensed Luxembourg notaries; Ministry of Justice standard-form model statutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Luxembourg notary or counsel to draft the articles of association (statuts). The draft must state the corporate object limited to software publishing, mobile application and hyper-casual game publishing; the EUR 12,000 share capital; the par value of each share (minimum EUR 1.00); the registered office address in Luxembourg; the management rules for the gérant (manager); the financial year; and the dissolution and wind-up rules. The notary reviews the draft for legal compliance and confirms the final version before signature.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association in French or English
Identity and proof of address of each shareholder
Corporate KYC bundle for any corporate founder (articles, RCS extract, beneficial-owner declaration)
Defined corporate-object wording aligned with ISIC 5820
Registered-office lease intent or address confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or counsel raises substantive objections, amend the draft articles and resubmit for a further conformity review; no public filing occurs at this stage, so corrections are private and without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked escrow account and deposit of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (e.g., BIL, BGL BNP Paribas, Société Générale Luxembourg, Spuerkees); any EU/EEA bank acceptable to the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a non-operational blocked account in the name of the 'SARL en formation' and deposit the full EUR 12,000 cash contribution. Instruct the bank to issue an attestation de blocage (blocked-funds certificate) addressed to the notary, confirming that the funds are irrevocably held in escrow for the future company and released only upon RCS registration. The bank performs full AML/KYC due diligence on the ultimate beneficial owners before accepting the deposit.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening form
AML/KYC questionnaire and beneficial-owner identification
Source-of-funds evidence
Final draft articles of association
Business plan describing hyper-casual game publishing and AdMob/AppLovin revenue flows
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional KYC or source-of-funds detail, furnish the requested corporate and personal documentation promptly or transfer the opening request to a second Luxembourg bank; a new or updated blocking certificate is then issued to the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Notaire) empowered to receive authentic acts and to file electronically with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend before the chosen notary with valid identification. The notary verifies the identity and legal capacity of each founder, reads the statutes aloud, confirms receipt of the attestation de blocage together with proof of full capital payment, and records the irrevocable subscription of the shares. All founders and the notary sign the acte constitutif. The notary then issues certified copies and initiates the electronic RCS filing workflow.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or EU national identity card of each founder
Original attestation de blocage from the bank
Final notarial deed and approved statutes
Corporate authorizing resolution of any corporate founder
Consent or lease evidencing the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect in the deed or attachments, cure the issue by executing a rectification addendum before signature or by rescheduling the notarial appointment with corrected documents; no public consequence arises because registration has not yet occurred.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing with the RCS and obtaining legal personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), eRCS electronic filing platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of signature, the notary submits the application for RCS registration through the eRCS platform, attaching the electronic copy of the authentic deed, the bank blocking certificate, the acceptance of office by the gérant, and the registered-office proof. The RCS verifies statutory conformity and registers the company on approval. Legal personality commences on the registration date, and the company receives its RCS number in the format B + six digits and a certified RCS extract.
required_dossiers: Authentic notarial deed in electronic form
eRCS registration application form
Bank blocked-funds certificate (attestation de blocage)
Statement of acceptance of office by the gérant
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues an incident or query, respond with corrections or supplementary documents through the eRCS portal within the stated deadline (typically one to two months). If refused, file a judicial appeal before the Luxembourg District Court within one month of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), accessible at resa.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the communication of the registered statutes with the RCS for publication in the RESA. The RCS publishes the communication electronically within two business days of registration. This publication makes the statutes enforceable against third parties (erga omnes effect). The publication service is free of charge since the 2016 reform.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Notarial communication form
Approved statutes text
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication is delayed or technically rejected, the notary refiles the corrected communication through the LBR; if substantive inconsistencies appear, a rectificative notarial deed must be executed and filed with the RCS before republication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation tax, VAT, social security and statistical registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); STATEC; commune of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the business registration with the AEDT for municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), corporate income tax and VAT; obtain the Luxembourg VAT number. Within eight days of any first hire, register as an employer with the CCSS and affiliate with the shared social security centre. Submit the STATEC economic census form and confirm the office lease with the competent commune. Finally, open an operational corporate bank account configured to receive AdMob and AppLovin advertising payouts.
required_dossiers: RCS extract dated less than three months
Articles of association and notarial deed
Manager (gérant) appointment and identity document
Registered-office lease agreement
AEDT VAT registration form (formulaire 102)
CCSS employer registration form
Operating bank account opening and KYC package
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT queries the VAT registration, submit proof of intended economic activity, expected turnover, and place of supply for digital advertising services. If CCSS registration is delayed, provisional affiliation may be granted retroactively upon submission of the employer form; follow up in writing to avoid late-payment assessments.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie), Direction générale de l'industrie et de la technologie; ISIC 5820 software publishing is not an industrial establishment under Luxembourg law
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required - the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to craft, merchant, industrial and liberal professions does not condition digital software and mobile-game publishing on an establishment permit; RCS registration and AEDT tax registration constitute the sole administrative authorizations for an office-only publisher

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement, Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - pure digital publishing is not listed in Annexes I or II of the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; no EIA, environmental permit, or environmental compliance plan is required for an office-only hyper-casual game publisher
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for production because the activity generates no industrial wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste. Operational duties are limited to municipal urban waste rules for office premises, including WEEE (Directive 2012/19/EU) sorting upon disposal of IT equipment, compliance with the landlord's energy and waste charter, and use of cloud-based hosting outside Luxembourg without local discharge exposure

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office-only clearance: no autorisation d'établissement recevant du public (ERP) is required unless a public showroom is opened; the landlord's fire-safety certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) covering the leased floor area must be attached to the office lease. The Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) receives the business registration through the RCS. Workplace duties under the Law of 17 June 1994 require fire extinguishers, marked emergency exits, electrical installation checks, a first-aid kit, and employee safety instruction. No industrial structural-load inspection is relevant to non-industrial digital operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; unified portal: guichet.lu / myguichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entity registers with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through RCS e-filing / guichet.lu, obtains RC number; then applies for a VAT identification number via Form 640A with AEDT; CIT identification aligns with the RC number for tax filings; a local tax representative may be required for non-resident taxable persons without permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election is available under Luxembourg law; SARL is per se subject to CIT/IRC; specific anti-hybrid elections under ATAD and deductible payments rules are limited to binding tax ruling procedures; optional VAT grouping and partial cooperation exemptions are available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 annual taxable turnover for established small taxpayers; non-established foreign suppliers generally must register immediately without threshold when supplying goods or services in Luxembourg
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No general mandatory real-time B2B e-invoicing/clearance regime; PEPPOL-BIS e-invoicing is mandatory for all B2G invoices (public sector) since 2022; B2B XML/structured e-invoicing optional. No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping scheme for hyper-casual gaming publishers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies on supplies of goods physically dispatched/transported outside the EU by the seller or for the seller, subject to proof of export within 90 days; also applies to ocean/air transport services and services directly connected with exported goods; B2B services to non-EU consumers located outside EU are also zero-rated under the place-of-supply rule.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Single Administrative Document/SAD) or electronic export summary declaration
Proof of physical dispatch: Bill of Lading / CMR / Air Waybill or carrier's attestation
Commercial invoice / contract evidencing the transfer of ownership to non-EU buyer
Bank transfer / inward remittance certificate evidencing actual cross-border payment
Customs export proof accepted by AEDT (all relevant ECS data)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities may claw back wrongly zero-rated VAT plus late interest and impose administrative fines between 10% and 100% of under-declared VAT; fraudulent export claims trigger criminal penalties of imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 250,000; the taxpayer bears the complete documentary burden for 10 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting as the national central bank and Eurosystem member; foreign exchange supervision is coordinated under the CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier) regulation of credit institutions and payments services.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility pursuant to the EU Treaty free movement of capital (TFEU Article 63) and the Eurosystem legal framework. No exchange control licences, quantitative limits, or import/export cover approvals apply to corporate treasury transactions in EUR or any convertible currency. Profit remittance from a SARL is through formal corporate distributions from distributable reserves, evidenced by a shareholders resolution and audited accounts where required, subject to a 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax that may be reduced under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (0% for a qualifying 10% participation held for at least 12 months) or under an applicable tax treaty. Interest and royalty payments generally are exempt from Luxembourg withholding tax, but typical corporate law formalities and transfer-pricing substance documentation remain mandatory to resist recharacterisation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation and no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds generated by the SARL. Receipts from ad-monetisation (AdMob, AppLovin, or other platforms) may be retained in EUR or designated foreign currency accounts held at a Luxembourg or EEA credit institution. The BCL only requires statistical balance-of-payments and international-investment-position reporting for cross-border transactions above filing thresholds; such reporting is informational and does not impose surrender or conversion obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for operational collection of small-ticket ad-network receipts and vendor disbursements; Low for capital-escrow applications and core treasury concentration. An EMI (Electronic Money Institution) must be passport-licensed in another EEA state under the PSD2 and registered with the CSSF if operating in Luxembourg. EMIs may issue e-money and provide payment accounts but cannot accept deposits, cannot grant credit, and their client funds have no Luxembourg deposit-guarantee protection under the LSP (Loi relative aux systèmes de garantie des dépôts). The SARL statutory capital and capital maintenance verification for the Luxembourg Commercial Register will only be safely achieved through a regulated credit institution rather than an EMI account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance of the SARL statutory manager(s) and every natural-person UBO owning at least 25% is generally required at the bank's Luxembourg premises before account finalisation. Several private banks and international groups permit a hybrid protocol: physical identification before the local notary or a Luxembourg-licensed KYC agent followed by a secure video interview with the banker. Fully remote onboarding is not the general rule; banks frequently insist on an in-person or high-assurance video interview addressing the commercial substance, funding sources, ad-network counterparties, and anticipated cross-border transaction volumes. Irrespective of format, the bank must establish direct contact with the decision-makers under CSSF AML/CFT expectations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-Luxembourg corporate or trustee shareholders creating an opaque UBO chain in jurisdictions perceived as high-risk or likely to be used for tax avoidance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete shareholding organizational chart down to natural persons, RCS Luxembourg incorporation file and articles, notarised share transfer and subscription agreements, UBO declaration compliant with Luxembourg law of 13 January 2019 on UBO register, current and clean registry extracts of each intermediate holding company, tax-residence certificates, and external counsel AML opinion demonstrating economic substance and ownership rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volumes of low-average-ticket credits from advertising platforms plus named payors not matching the SARL's direct contractual counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Google AdMob and AppLovin monetisation agreements, SDK/API integration registration showing the SARL as developer and payee, consolidated payout statements from ad networks with counterparty reference, merchant ID, and settlement ledger, bank statements covering the prior 6 months, and an internal treasury policy describing platform-to-bankflow and interposing licensees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid inbound capital followed immediately by outbound disbursements to non-Luxembourg subcontracting game developers, affiliate marketers, or intellectual-property holding companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully signed development, marketing subcontractor and IP license agreements, invoices and work delivery reports with app-store version evidence, proof of copyright ownership and trademark registration, domain and infrastructure hosting contracts, VAT invoices with Luxembourg VAT identification where applicable, and transfer pricing documentation following OECD TP principles for the royalty or service fee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of fintech EMI balances, virtual-asset conversion, or settlement routes not through a full credit institution, raising layering red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Policy that all business settlement must run through a Luxembourg or EEA-licensed credit institution using SWIFT MT103/SEPA rails; no virtual-asset exposure; documented screen-only exemption for ad-platform merchant statements; certified payment service utilisation report; and compliance certification signed by the COO supporting avoidance of unaccounted pass-through transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance mismatch from a newly incorporated Luxembourg SARL with no physical office, no local employees or directors beyond nominee, and all decision-taking abroad.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg lease agreement for registered office, payroll and social security registrations, local statutory manager agreement with professional liability coverage, minutes of board meetings held in Luxembourg, tax and VAT filings proving economic activity, local accountant/auditor engagement letter, and annual accounts filed at the RCS Luxembourg.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for a Luxembourg SARL capital injection is a SWIFT MT103 credit from the shareholder's bank to the SARL's euro settlement account at a Luxembourg or EEA credit institution. The beneficiary field must contain the exact Luxembourg IBAN and the SARL legal name as inscribed in the RCS Luxembourg. The payment reference should read 'Capital increase – Luxembourg SARL – [shareholder name] – [deed date] – shares issued' or, if made through an international bank processing through a correspondent loop, the reference should be kept concise to avoid truncation.The remitting bank must attribute the correct BCL/ECB balance-of-payments purpose code for direct-investment equity flow; in practice the bank's corporate department will accept 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital' (or a bank-defined code with that semantic) after receiving the notarised share subscription deed and the statutory deposit certificate issued by the receiving credit institution. No prior BCL authorisation is required, but the receiving bank may require proof of identification of the payer and a copy of the notarised capital increase to clear anti-money-laundering verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements and operational out-payments, the SARL will use the SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT/SCT Inst) for EUR disbursements to EEA beneficiaries and SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA or foreign-currency payments. For high-value or documentary transactions—such as acquisition of substantial game-source code, exclusive IP purchase, or infrastructure equipment—a Commercial Letter of Credit (documentary LC) can be opened by the bank under the SARL's credit lines, supported by invoices, bills of lading, or digital acceptance certificates. Routine royalty payments to overseas game developers under license agreements are typically executed via MT103 with descriptive references matching the underlying contract version and date; verification checks include the ICC Sanctions List, OFAC/UE/UN sanctions screening, counterparty KYC, and reference to the Luxembourg domestic VAT declarations if the service is subject to reverse-charge.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC deliverable FX forward contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/JPY) transacted with a Luxembourg or EEA credit institution under ISDA/ EMIR margining rules

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted to currencies with limited liquidity or capital-control regimes, limited to hedges of genuine commercial receivables/payables and subject to counterparty credit limits
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD or EUR/GBP) for matching medium-term intercompany loans and fund-flows in excess of 12 months
FX call options and zero-cost collars for hedging ad-network revenue and marketing cost volatility without speculative intent
Exchange-traded futures contracts on EUR/USD and EUR/JPY for short-term treasury adjustments if Eurex-clearing membership is available through a bank broker

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (annual accounts) and approval minutes filed with the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve the annual accounts within six months of the financial year-end (by 30 June for a calendar-year SARL); the approved accounts must be filed with the RCS within one month after approval (by 31 July for a calendar-year SARL; a reasoned extension may be requested up to 31 October).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an automatic reminder and administrative fines from EUR 500 to EUR 2,500; continued non-filing after the legal deadline exposes the SARL to judicial action and administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS maintenance fee (taxe annuelle for electronic registration and company file)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable annually by 31 January of each calendar year; for the first registration year the fee is prorated from the date of enrolment.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment leads to a formal reminder and accrual of late-interest; persistent default for two consecutive years results in administrative strike-off of the company from the RCS and loss of legal standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 563/563bis) covering Luxembourg corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC) and related computations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg direct tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year SARL: file by 30 September of the following year; an automatic extension to 31 December is generally granted for electronic filings; further extension may be obtained with a justified written request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing imposes a surcharge of 10% of the assessed corporate income tax (minimum EUR 1,000); default interest accrues at 0.5% per month; additional administrative penalties up to EUR 1,500 apply for serious delay.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax return (impôt sur la fortune) and declaration of taxable net assets
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg direct tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing deadline is aligned with the corporate income tax return: 30 September of the following year for calendar-year SARL, with electronic extension to 31 December; net wealth tax becomes payable upon issuance of the assessment notice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid net wealth tax attracts monthly default interest of 0.5%; late filing or declaration is subject to the same administrative penalties as income tax, including surcharges and forced recovery proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership information (UBO / RBE annual certification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of the initial RBE registration in each calendar year; any change in beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual confirmation is subject to a reminder and may be prosecuted under the law of 13 January 2019; sanctions include administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 for legal entities, potential restriction on corporate distributions and notarial acts, and court-ordered rectification.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit of the annual accounts is required if the SARL exceeds two of the three following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets exceeding EUR 4.4 million, net turnover exceeding EUR 8.8 million, or average workforce exceeding 50 employees. Small companies that remain below these thresholds are exempt from statutory audit; audit is also mandatory for public interest entities and for entities forming part of a group that is required to prepare consolidated financial statements above the harmonized EU thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as defined by the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial ledgers and annual accounts (Règlement grand-ducal implementing the EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU) must be used for individual statutory accounts. IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for consolidated accounts of listed groups and is mandatory for public interest entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Luxembourg Law of 13 January 2019, the SARL must certify the accuracy of the beneficial owners recorded in the RBE at least once every calendar year. The annual confirmation is completed online via the LBR RBE portal within 30 days of the anniversary of the initial registration. A supplementary update is mandatory within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership, including any transfer of shares resulting in a shareholder reaching, exceeding, or ceasing to exceed the 25% ownership threshold.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - 3,500 per year for a Luxembourg registered office and corporate administrative agent; a full domiciliation and outsourced corporate secretary package typically ranges from USD 2,200 to 4,500.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 15,000 for a compulsory statutory audit when the SARL exceeds the size thresholds; no audit fee is incurred for small exempt companies, but a voluntary audit may cost USD 4,000 - 12,000 depending on transactional volume and complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate standard rate (Luxembourg City: 17% corporate income tax, 7% solidarity surcharge, and 6.75% municipal business tax; non-city municipal multipliers may vary)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains; 80% net IP income exemption under the Luxembourg IP box; notional interest deduction for equity-financed assets; no withholding tax on interest and royalties under local statutory law; ATAD-compliant interest limitation rules apply

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 851 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur la société et pour l'impôt commercial communal); filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu and the Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes) e-filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For financial years ending on 31 December, the return is due by 31 December of the immediately following calendar year; earlier deadlines may be set by taxpayer-specific tax assessment notices; extensions are available on reasoned written request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, RCS number, and full address of the LU SARL
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must correspond exactly to the Luxembourg trade and companies register; non-resident directors must ensure the local registered agent confirms consistency before e-filing

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable year and fiscal-reporting period; identify any short-period return
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a hyper-casual games studio, the period must match audited/provisional accounts closed under LUX GAAP; indicate if the company uses calendar-year accounting

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or net loss reported in the balance sheet/P&L account
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back local statutory, ad valorem, and non-deductible taxes; reconcile GAAP profit to commercial taxable base excluding participation-exempt income and IP-box exempt revenues

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses: hidden profit distributions, secret commissions, excess interest on shareholder loans, and fines
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List amounts paid directly or indirectly to foreign group digital ads intermediaries (e.g. AdMob, AppLovin) if any part is identified as disguised royalty or excess remuneration

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income from advertising and in-app purchases operationalized under the AdMob/AppLovin payout rails
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Taxable business income in Luxembourg; app-store payouts must be recorded gross, with remaining profit attributable to the SARL based on substance and risk profile

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying IP Box deduction: 80% of net income derived from qualifying intangible assets
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply only where the hyper-casual game IP was created by the SARL under an eligible beneficial-development activity; must be supported by qualifying expenditure reports and nexus ratio records

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholder loan interest paid to a non-resident creditor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the borrower/creditor relationship, arm's-length interest rate, loan agreement, and proof of no statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on interest

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemptions, controlled foreign corporation disclosures, and any aggregated related-party transaction schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Required even when no exemption claimed; identify global distributors and licensing entities located in lower-tax jurisdictions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts default administrative penalties up to 10% of assessed tax, plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.6% on the outstanding corporate income tax and municipal business tax; in material cases, criminal fines and director disqualification may follow
